# Stack 04 — generation (04a ∥ 04b)

**Nothing is waiting on Kent. He answered everything on 2026-09-17** — six questions and eight small corrections, after a read-only design review. The answers are in **`plans/notes/2026-09-17-kent-decisions-stack-04.md`** (rows G1–G6 and S1–S8), they are binding, and this plan has been rewritten in place to match them. In one breath: **no ensemble** — the model's stated range, labelled (record 0015, G1); **"This happened" is fixed by counting only the versions that survived** (G2), and a claim moved only by reweighting says so in the Inspector (G3); **up to three silent retries after a refusal** (G4); **$500 for the stack, a $15 hard stop per run in code, and only the coordinator spends money** (G5); **Hormuz recorded early, all four once the prompt is frozen** (G6).

---

**Goal:** type any sentence and watch a real map build itself, one claim at a time, with evidence — and with no key, watch the same thing play from a recording. After this stack the four example hypotheses from `ASSIGNMENT.md` all open, the numbers on screen are the engine's, and every proposal the validator refused is visible on the way past.

**What this stack must not do.** No thesis card, no stop-loss, no tail strip, no live market prices (stack 05). No storage — nothing is kept between requests except what a running process holds in memory; the SQLite file is stack 05's (FR-31). No `refine`, no probes, no feedback-arrow unrolling (stack 06). **No re-prompting for a whole map**, ever (anti-pattern 2). **The model never mints an identifier, never declares its own provenance, and never decides whether a map is legal** (anti-pattern 1, record 0003). No ensemble and no graph-to-graph reconciliation — record 0015 (Kent, G1). No pastcast (FR-30, stack 07).

**Rests on:** record **0006** (the model boundary — the SDK, the model, structured output, one proposal per call, the web-search tool, the cached system prompt, refusals shown not hidden), **0008** (five testing layers; recorded responses; evals out of band), **0012** (replay mode, accepted 2026-09-17 — built here), **0003** (the model proposes, our code disposes), **0014** (what it defers to 04: the provenance-derived spread on arrow strengths, and the open question that became record 0015, accepted 2026-09-17), **0005** (link semantics), **0010** (grounding; mostly stack 05, but FR-28's search at generation time is here). Read each record's "Decision Outcome" before writing a line.

> ### Before any code that calls Claude, load the `claude-api` skill.
> Model names, request shapes, parameter names and prices change, and memory is unreliable. **Record 0006 holds the verified specifics** — the client library, the model name, the structured-output call, the thinking setting, the server-side web-search tool name, the cache-control block, the refusal stop reason. **Verify every one of them against the skill before typing it**, and put the price table in exactly one module with the date it was read beside it. This plan deliberately contains no model name, no parameter and no dollar figure. Every agent's brief carries this paragraph.

---

## How 04a and 04b stay out of each other's way

Two stacks, in parallel, as 03a ∥ 03b ran. **04a is the browser; 04b is the server.** The split of every file that could collide:

| File or tree | Owner this cycle | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `frontend/src/**` except `api/schema.ts` | **04a** | 04b never edits a component, a hook or a stylesheet |
| `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` | **04b** | Only 04b runs `make types`, once, in its top pull request. A `schema.ts` diff on a 04a branch is a mistake to revert — **with one exception: 04a's bottom pull request, the engine fix (agent F), regenerates it for the one new field on a diff row** |
| `backend/**`, `evals/**`, `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.env.example` | **04b** | 04a never edits a Python file — **except agent F, in 04a's bottom pull request, which owns `domain/diff.py` and its tests for that pull request only** |
| `spec/workbench/**` | **04a** | Including the new `streaming-growth.md` |
| `spec/generation/**`, `docs/adr/**` | **04b** | |
| `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` | **04b**, in its top pull request only | 04b's agent writes the browser sentences from 04a's merged state, so **04a merges first** |

**04a's first three pull requests merge first** (the fix, the chapter, the join). They need nothing from 04b to be correct, and they unblock Kent's eye on real computed numbers days before the model pipeline exists. **04a's last pull request — the growing canvas — is held until 04b's stream pull request is on `main`** (S6): its browser test plays a recording through a route 04b owns, **Add a claim** calls 04b's `POST /api/generate/insert`, and the `e2e` job runs every spec, so merging it early turns `main` red. When 04b's top pull request is ready, rebase its branch onto the finished `main` rather than merging `main` into it — a linear child restacks itself (STATUS, 2026-09-17).

**The one true dependency:** 04a's third pull request draws a map as it streams, and the stream is 04b's. It is handled three ways and no other. (i) **The event vocabulary is settled in this plan**, below, and pasted into both stacks' briefs — the shapes-sheet trick from stack 02. (ii) 04a types the events by hand in `frontend/src/stream/events.ts`, exactly as stack 03b hand-typed `WorldView`; 04b's top pull request regenerates `schema.ts` and adds a **type-level test** that fails if the two drift. (iii) The 04a growth agent is launched in wave 2, after 04b's stream route is green on its branch, and develops against a server run out of the 04b worktree — read-only, no edits, no shared files.

---

## The pull requests

### Stack 04a — the join and the growing canvas

| # | Branch → base | Contents |
|---|---------------|----------|
| 0 | `fix/04-observe-direction` → `main` | **The engine fix both stacks stand on (G2, G3).** The dated amendment to record 0014; `spec/multiverse/diff.md` open question 7 closed and the reweighting paragraph added; `domain/diff.py` — the direction is read with the same weights the number was read with, and a diff row says when a claim moved only by reweighting; tests; regenerated `schema.ts` |
| 1 | `spec/04a-streaming-growth` → #0 | **Docs only.** `spec/workbench/streaming-growth.md`; the chapter table in `spec/workbench/README.md`; close `diff-view.md` open question 1, `inspector.md` open questions 2 and 3, and `diff.md` open question 5 in place; the Inspector's reweighting sentence (G3) |
| 2 | `feat/04a-join` → #1 | `ApiWorldSource` switched on. Number slots fill; the fifth diff state `shifted`; the rail ranks; the computed chip sentence; the lazy conditional on a wire's midpoint; the six buttons move numbers; the retraction badge read off the world |
| 3 | `feat/04a-growth` → #2 | The stream reader; skeleton tiles; growth with pinned layout; wires in causal order; chips last; the input bar (hypothesis, Verify target, the likelihood slider with "I don't know"); the launchpad's three cards live; the receipt strip; the `no_path` card; the replay badge |

### Stack 04b — the model pipeline, the stream, and the evidence it works

| # | Branch → base | Contents |
|---|---------------|----------|
| 1 | `spec/04b-generation` → `main` | **Docs only.** `spec/generation/{proposals,grounding,streaming,replay,evaluation}.md`; the landing page's chapter table; **decision record 0015**, status `accepted` (Kent, 2026-09-17, G1); the dated amendment to record 0003 (G4); FR-8 and PRD §13 amended to match (S7) |
| 2 | `feat/04b-pipeline` → #1 | `engine/proposal.py`, `engine/prompt.py`, `engine/expand.py`, `engine/receipt.py`, `engine/pricing.py`. Stop rules, the Verify door, `no_path`, grounding, provenance written by us. The boundary cassettes |
| 3 | `feat/04b-stream` → #2 | `api/generate.py` — the event stream and two more routes. `engine/transcript.py`, `engine/replay.py`, `backend/recordings/*.jsonl`, `make record-demo`, the `recordings` job in continuous integration |
| 4 | `feat/04b-evals` → #3 | `evals/`, `make eval`. **No ensemble (G1).** The provenance-derived spread on arrow strengths, **with the chapter sweep in the same pull request**. Regenerated `schema.ts`. `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` |

---

## The shapes sheet — the event vocabulary both stacks build against

Settled here so two stacks cannot answer the same small question twice. **Eight events.** Each is one `event:` name with one JSON `data:` payload, in `backend/src/katalyst/engine/events.py`, mirrored by hand in `frontend/src/stream/events.ts`.

```python
class GenerationStarted(BaseModel):     # event: generation_started
    generation_id: str                  # minted by engine/ids.py
    seed: int                           # what domain/ will propagate with
    hypothesis: str                     # the sentence the user typed
    target: str | None                  # the Verify door's destination, in their words
    # mode, the recording date and the prompt hash are on Receipt and nowhere else (S3)

class ProposalAccepted(BaseModel):      # event: proposal_accepted
    at: int                             # position in the transcript, from 0
    proposition: Proposition | None     # the new claim, identifier minted here
    links: tuple[Link, ...]             # its incoming arrows, identifiers minted here
    frontier: tuple[PropositionId, ...] # claims still open to expand

class ProposalRejected(BaseModel):      # event: proposal_rejected
    at: int
    claim_in_words: str                 # what the model wrote. Never minted, never drawn as a tile
    violations: tuple[Violation, ...]   # domain/validity.py's own codes and sentences
    frontier: tuple[PropositionId, ...] # claims still open — BOTH growth events say it, so a claim closed
                                        # by its third refusal loses its skeleton at once (review, 2026-09-17)

class BeliefsPropagated(BaseModel):     # event: beliefs_propagated
    world: World                        # the whole thing, from domain/propagate

class Verdict(BaseModel):               # event: verdict — Verify door only
    kind: Literal["reached", "no_path"]
    path: tuple[PropositionId, ...]     # empty on no_path
    product: float | None               # the multiplied-out likelihood of that path (INV-8)
    nearest: PropositionId | None       # on no_path: the closest claim the map did reach
    why: str                            # one plain sentence

class Receipt(BaseModel):               # event: receipt  (NFR-6)
    model: str
    calls: int
    input_tokens: int
    output_tokens: int
    cache_read_tokens: int
    searches: int                       # web searches this run made — billed apart from tokens, so
                                        # `dollars` cannot be re-derived without it (review, 2026-09-17)
    dollars: float
    seconds: float
    mode: Literal["live", "replay"]
    recording_date: date | None
    prompt_hash: str

class Done(BaseModel):                  # event: done
    reason: Literal["reached_terminal", "depth_cap", "width_cap", "claim_cap",
                    "spend_cap", "refusal_cap", "no_terminal"]
                                        # ONE RULE (proposals.md B4): the reason names what closed the LAST open claim —
                                        # an ending or a Stop -> reached_terminal; a cap -> that cap (three refusals in a
                                        # row is the refusal cap; it was "model_stopped", but the model did not stop);
                                        # spend_cap and no_terminal override
                                        # no "search_cap": reaching the search cap stops SEARCHING, not the
                                        # generation (later arrows are `argued`), so it is never a stop reason
                                        # why the GENERATION stopped. "no_path" is on Verdict only (S3)
    claims: int
    links: int
    rejected: int

class Failed(BaseModel):                # event: failed
    message: str                        # one plain sentence. Never a stack trace
```

**The transport is `POST /api/generate` read as a stream, not `EventSource`** (*decided here*). Two reasons, both hard: the request carries a hypothesis, an optional target, an optional user belief and a seed, and `EventSource` can only send a GET with no body; and `EventSource` reconnects by itself, which would silently re-run a generation and spend the money twice. The browser uses `fetch` and reads the body. The wire format is still server-sent events — `event:` and `data:` lines — so the format stays inspectable in a terminal with `curl`.

**Four things the cross-chapter review settled (2026-09-17), binding on both stacks.** (1) **A `Stop` and a closed claim make no event of their own.** A `Stop` leaves a transcript line; the next growth event's `frontier` no longer names that claim, and on `beliefs_propagated` **every skeleton goes** — the frontier is empty by definition — so no rectangle ever stands where nothing will arrive. (2) **Which recording plays:** the replayer matches the request's `hypothesis` against each recording's `generation_started.hypothesis`, exact after trimming surrounding spaces; nothing matches → one plain sentence, never a guess. (3) **Readiness says what can be replayed:** `Readiness.replayable: tuple[RecordingSummary, ...]`, `RecordingSummary{example: str, recording_date: date}` — one name, `recording_date`, everywhere. (4) **Anything that is not an accepted proposal counts toward the three in a row** — a validator rejection, a vendor refusal, a malformed answer — one rule, not three.

**A recording is this same stream, line for line** — `backend/recordings/<example>.jsonl`, one JSON object per line, in order, with a header line carrying the base map, the seed, the date and the prompt hash (record 0012). On replay every event is re-emitted unchanged **except two (S4)**: `receipt` is **rebuilt** with `mode: "replay"`, zero dollars, and the recording's date and hash; and `beliefs_propagated` is **recomputed** — the recording carries the seed, `domain/` re-propagates, and **a recording therefore holds no `World` at all**, which keeps the file small and makes replay and live agree by construction. Record 0012 names only four event types; the chapter must say all eight and say this.

---

## 04a pull request 0 — the engine fix both stacks stand on (G2, G3)

**What is wrong, measured** (Hormuz, seed 20261001, `Observe(target="B", value=True)`, the shipped 2 000 versions × 8 worlds; re-run by the coordinator on 2026-09-17): **209 of the 2 000 versions have no surviving world.** Such a version reports `0.0` (`domain/propagation.py`, `_per_version`) and counts for nothing in the number and the band, because its weight is zero (`_draw`). But `_agreement_on` in `domain/diff.py` takes a plain unweighted mean of the signs, so each dead version **votes against the direction**. M1 and M2 both read 89.05% against the 90% bar, both read `unchanged`, the rail is empty, and **This happened** looks like a button that does nothing. Counted with the weights: **98.66%** (99.44% among survivors).

**The rule (Kent, G2): read the direction with the same weights the number was read with.** `_agreement_on` takes the version weights; its two callers, `_states` and `_ranked_endings`, already hold them. Under the five edits that are not an observation every weight is 1, so not one bit moves anywhere else — **pin that with a test that compares a non-observe diff with itself before and after the change, never with a typed-in number.** Worlds per version stays 8. The 90% bar is untouched.

**A claim moved only by reweighting (Kent, G3).** Observing C moves H from `.356` to `.365`, nearly twice the 0.005 floor, and H's same-direction share is zero **by construction**: H has no causes, so inside every version its answer is its own prior in both worlds and the paired difference is exactly zero. The diff states stay as they are. The diff's row for such a claim gains **one field** saying so (the agent names it from `spec/vocabulary.md`'s words and says why), and the Inspector prints one sentence, word for word: ***"this claim moved only because the observation made some versions count more."*** The same shape as K4 — a fact about the reading lives in the Inspector.

**In this pull request:** the dated amendment to record 0014 (dated in place, as record 0008 was — nothing in the decision changed; say what was measured and the one rule); `spec/multiverse/diff.md` open question 7 closed in place, the rule stated once, the reweighting paragraph added, and **every same-direction percentage the chapter quotes re-measured from the engine** (list which moved); `domain/diff.py`; tests `test_an_observation_puts_a_row_on_the_rail` · `test_a_dead_version_does_not_vote` · `test_direction_is_read_with_the_numbers_own_weights` · `test_an_edit_that_is_not_an_observation_is_unchanged_by_the_weights` · `test_a_claim_moved_only_by_reweighting_says_so`; `make types` and the regenerated `frontend/src/api/schema.ts`. `mypy --strict` clean, `domain/` stays at 100%.

---

## 04a pull request 1 — `streaming-growth.md`, and four questions closed

Chapter shape from `spec/README.md`: Purpose · Data model · Behaviour · INVARIANTS · ANTI-PATTERNS · Open questions. Plain words; every invariant names the component test or the numbered line of the visual review checklist that checks it. Local numbers continue the workbench series (`tiles-ports-wires.md` holds 1–12, `color-motion-type.md` 13–19; count the rest off the merged chapters and carry on).

**`streaming-growth.md` must settle:**

- **The loading state is the map growing** (UX-8, FR-5). There is no spinner anywhere, and a skeleton tile is on screen before the first model call returns — which is what NFR-7's "first paint within a second" actually means here, because one proposal takes seconds to come back (record 0006). Say so; NFR-7's words "of the first token" do not fit a pipeline that returns whole proposals, and the chapter corrects them.
- **A skeleton tile is a reserved rectangle, not a shimmer.** It is the claim's box at the layer the engine says it belongs to, drawn at the tile's own clamped height, with the layer's name and nothing else. It never animates beyond an opacity change.

## 04b pull request 2 — the pipeline

```python
# engine/proposal.py — what the model is allowed to return. One of three.
class ClaimProposal(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["claim"]
    claim: str                       # the sentence, as a person would say it
    claim_kind: Literal["event", "market", "not_tradeable"]
    resolution: Resolution           # criteria, judge, resolve-by (INV-1)
    prior: Ranged                    # p, lo, hi. No owner field: we stamp "model"
    base_rate: BaseRate | None
    payoff: ContractPayoff | PricePayoff | None   # required when claim_kind == "market"
    not_tradeable_reason: str | None              # required when claim_kind == "not_tradeable"
    cause: str                       # the identifier of a claim ALREADY on the map
    link: LinkDraft                  # the arrow from that cause into this new claim

class LinkProposal(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["link"]
    source: str                      # both ends already on the map
    target: str
    link: LinkDraft

class Stop(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["stop"]
    why: str                         # one sentence, shown in the transcript

class LinkDraft(BaseModel):
    mode: Literal["trigger", "sustain"]
    strength: float
    lag: int
    shape: Literal["impulse", "step", "ramp"]
    half_life: int | None
    rationale: str
    sources: tuple[SourceDraft, ...] # NO provenance field, and no identifier field

Proposal = Annotated[ClaimProposal | LinkProposal | Stop, Field(discriminator="kind")]
```

**Three things the model is structurally unable to do**, because the fields do not exist: mint an identifier, declare its own provenance, and return more than one thing. A new claim's identifier is minted by `engine/ids.py`; an existing claim is named by an identifier the prompt handed it; `owner="model"` is stamped by us; and **provenance is decided by us from what actually happened** — at least one cited source **that the search tool itself returned in that call** → `documented` (S1: a URL the model typed that the tool never returned is not a source, and is dropped with a note in the transcript); a rationale with no such source → `argued`; neither → `asserted`. `historical` and `market_implied` come from stack 05's adapters and never from a proposal.

```python
# engine/expand.py
def expand(graph: Graph, frontier: PropositionId, *, target: str | None) -> Outcome
```

One call, one proposal, then `domain.validate` on the map the proposal would leave behind. Accepted → mint, emit `proposal_accepted`. Rejected → emit `proposal_rejected` with **every** violation, and never repair. Both are events; both go in the transcript. **After a refusal the engine asks again for the same frontier claim, up to three times in a row, and the next call is never told what was wrong (Kent, G4)** — violation text never enters a prompt.

**The caps, all arguments with these defaults** (*decided here*): depth 5 layers · width 3 children per claim · 30 claims in total · 3 refusals in a row on one frontier claim closes that claim · 3 frontier claims expanded concurrently · **a cap on web searches per generation (S2; the agent picks the default and justifies it in `proposals.md`)** · **a spending cap per run, default $15 (G5)**. Record 0006 *estimates* a 30-claim map at about 40 calls; the first real measurement goes in `STATUS.md`.

**Two stop rules that are not caps.** A generation ends at `reached_terminal` when every open frontier claim has closed and the map has at least one `market` or `not_tradeable` ending (INV-9). If the caps are hit with no ending at all, the engine makes **one last call per open claim asking only for an ending** — and if that still fails, the stream ends `no_terminal` and the browser says so honestly. The engine never writes a claim the model did not propose.

**The Verify door.** The destination is added to the map up front as an ordinary claim; every call is told what it is; expansion is steered toward it. `no_path` is returned when the caps are hit and no path from the hypothesis reaches it, naming the nearest claim that was reached. **A bridge is never invented** — there is no code path that adds an arrow to make a path exist, and the eval case whose destination is unreachable proves it.

**Cost, and the hard stop (G5).** `engine/receipt.py` folds every call's usage into one `Receipt`, **and the pipeline checks the running receipt against the run's spending cap after every call**: over the cap, the generation ends `done.reason = "spend_cap"` with a plain sentence naming what was spent and what was got. The cap across runs ($500 for the stack) is a working agreement kept in `STATUS.md` — nothing is stored between runs until stack 05. **Only the coordinator runs a command that spends money; no sub-agent ever holds the key.** The pipeline agent builds against hand-written fake responses, adds `make record-cassettes`, and stops; the coordinator records. `engine/pricing.py` holds the price table and **nothing else**, with the day it was read and the `claude-api` skill named in a comment. A run whose cache reads stay at zero is a bug, not a slow day.

Every number the Strait of Hormuz example quotes
================================================

Generated. Do not edit this file by hand — `make numbers` writes it, and the
build fails when what is committed differs from what the program prints. The
program is `backend/src/katalyst/engine/worked_numbers.py`; it runs the shipped
engine on the stored example at the example's own seed and the shipped loop
sizes, and reads nothing but what comes back.

**A chapter quotes a number only where this file is one link away.** Cite a line
by the name at its start — `B · base · reading` — rather than restating the
figure, so that the day the arithmetic changes there is one place to look and one
diff to review.

Two parts, and the difference between them matters:

  INPUTS     numbers a person typed, in backend/src/katalyst/fixtures/hormuz.py.
             Stable. Safe to quote. A sweep that rewrites these is touching
             numbers that never needed touching.
  COMPUTED   numbers the engine worked out from those. Nobody typed one. These
             all move together the day the arithmetic changes.

Every line has three fields: the name, then what the product would show on screen
for this fact, then the fact itself. A `—` in the middle field means the product
does not render this fact at all — a move, a share of a band and how often the
versions agreed are real quantities, and none of them is a likelihood.

Five decimal places is a choice about reading. The screen never shows more than
two significant figures, and the rules layer will not call a claim *shifted*
until it has moved by 0.005, so five places hides nothing anybody could act on
while keeping a diff of this file readable.

**The digits are not what makes this file reproducible.** `make numbers-check`
is. It works every number out afresh and compares numbers **as numbers**, with
room for the last-bit disagreement between one machine's maths library and
another's, and compares every word, date and state character for character. That
is why the middle field is not compared as text: a number two machines agree
about to eight decimal places can still round two ways, and neither is wrong.
Each such number is checked at full precision on the line that owns it.

A `—` in the printed column means the product has no way of writing that kind of
number yet: a move, a share of a band, and how often the versions agreed are all
real quantities, and none of them is a likelihood.

[project]
name = "katalyst"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Turns a plain-English hypothesis into a cause-and-effect map that ends in trades."
requires-python = "==3.12.*"
dependencies = [
    # The web framework. It also publishes a machine-readable description of
    # every route and every data shape, which the browser app turns into
    # TypeScript types.
    "fastapi>=0.118,<1.0",
    # The server that runs the web framework. The "standard" extra adds the
    # file watcher used during development.
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.38,<1.0",
    # Defines and checks the shape of our data. Version 2 or later.
    "pydantic>=2.12,<3.0",
    # Reads environment variables into one settings object. See settings.py.
    "pydantic-settings>=2.12,<3.0",
    # Graph algorithms: finding loops, listing everything downstream of a node.
    "networkx>=3.5,<4.0",
    # Arrays and arithmetic for propagating beliefs.
    "numpy>=2.3,<3.0",
    # Mints identifiers that are unique without any central register and that

    Returns:
        The number as it is written on screen: `.35`, or `<.01`, or `>.99`.

    if not math.isfinite(likelihood):
        raise ValueError(
            "a likelihood to be written on screen must be a real number between 0 and 1; "
            f"got {likelihood!r}, which cannot be rounded to two significant figures"

    if likelihood <= 0.0:

    if likelihood >= 1.0:
        return ">.99"

    # point sits: `.995` becomes the digits 995 with its leading digit at the
    # first place after the point.

    # under `<.01`.

"""A belief: a likelihood with an honest range and a name on it.

A bare number on a box is a claim from nowhere. A belief is a likelihood that
says whose it is and how sure it is: a value between 0 and 1, a range around it,
and an owner — the model, the user, or a market. Every claim on the map carries
up to three of them side by side, and they are never combined into one.

That is the product in one design choice. The model's .61, the market's .48 and
your own .30 on the same claim are not three attempts at one true number to be
averaged away. They are the disagreement you are about to trade: model minus
market is the edge, user minus model is the argument you are having with the
tool.

Both classes here are frozen — once built, an instance cannot be changed. A
change is a new instance, recorded as an intervention on a branch.
"""

from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, model_validator


class Belief(BaseModel):
    """A likelihood with an honest range and a name on it.

    `p` is the likelihood, `lo` and `hi` are the range around it, and `owner`
    says whose number this is. There are exactly three owners and no code path
    ever combines two of them into one number.

    A belief is a number, never text. This layer does not round it and does not
    store it as a string; rounding happens once, at the moment of display.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    # Open question 1 in spec/graph/belief.md: a belief records no provenance,
    # so a model number anchored on a documented count and one asserted from
    # nothing look alike. Owner is not yet the whole answer.
    p: float = Field(
        ge=0.0,
        le=1.0,
        description=(
            "How likely the claim is to come out true, from 0 (certainly not) to 1 (certainly yes)."
        ),
    )
    lo: float = Field(
        ge=0.0,
        le=1.0,
        description="The bottom of the honest range around `p`. Never above `p`.",
    )
    hi: float = Field(
        ge=0.0,
        le=1.0,
        description="The top of the honest range around `p`. Never below `p`.",
    )
    owner: Literal["model", "user", "market"] = Field(
        description=(
            "Whose number this is: the model's estimate, the user's own, or a live "
            "price at a venue."
        ),
    )

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _range_is_ordered(self) -> "Belief":
        """Check that low is at most the likelihood, which is at most high.

        The field bounds above already cover 0 and 1; this covers the order.

        Returns:
            This same belief, once the order has been checked.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the three numbers are not in order.
        """
        if not (self.lo <= self.p <= self.hi):
            raise ValueError(
                "a belief must satisfy low <= likelihood <= high; got "
                f"low={self.lo}, likelihood={self.p}, high={self.hi}"
            )
        return self


class Beliefs(BaseModel):
    """The three voices on one claim: the model's, the user's, and a market's.

    Three named slots, deliberately not a dictionary, so that nothing can loop
    over them and average them by accident. `model` is always present. `user` is
    absent until the user says what they think. `market` is absent when no venue
    quotes this claim — and absent means the words "no market", never a blank and
    never a stand-in number.

    The field named `model` is legal. Pydantic protects names beginning with
    `model_`, so `model_config` and `model_dump` are reserved; plain `model` is
    not one of them. It stays `model` because that is the word the shared
    vocabulary uses, on the canvas and in the code alike.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    model: Belief = Field(
        description=(
            "What the model thinks, with this claim's causes taken into account. Always present."
        ),
    )
    user: Belief | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "What the user thinks. Written only by the `believe` intervention. None means "
            "the user has not said."
        ),
    )
    market: Belief | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "What a venue is currently pricing, read live and read-only. None means no "
            "venue quotes this claim."
        ),
    )

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _owners_match_slots(self) -> "Beliefs":
        """Check that each slot holds a belief owned by the voice the slot is named for.

        A belief sitting in the wrong slot would make the never-merge rule
        unenforceable: a user's number could sit in the model's chip and nothing
        would notice.

        Returns:
            This same set of beliefs, once every slot has been checked.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If any slot holds a belief owned by someone else.
        """
        for slot, belief in (("model", self.model), ("user", self.user), ("market", self.market)):
            if belief is not None and belief.owner != slot:
                raise ValueError(f"the '{slot}' slot holds a belief owned by '{belief.owner}'")
        return self
